disposition.summary: Scoped commit-parent source and recorded local compilation/source-control results support acceptance for lead integration. No fresh native evidence or issue closure is accepted.

required_tests: Thousands of share/cancel cycles show stable allocations under Instruments/leaks.
Success, cancellation, timeout, no-window and late/duplicate callbacks drop each owner exactly once.
ASan/native stress with concurrent requests validates no UAF or double-free after cleanup.
Cancel scope while picker open and verify prompt cleanup without occupying an IO worker until timeout.
Repeated requests, unavailable keyWindow/contentView, timeout, spurious wake and late callback.
Stress a bounded pool and assert exactly-once terminal result with balanced native lifetime.
iOS Mail subject for text, URL, single and multiple files.
Web payload inspection verifies title/file fields; unsupported metadata is documented.
Desktop native/fallback subject behavior is explicit and tested where implementable.

pending_native_and_closure_gates.issue_150: No service/recipient-delivery acceptance; subject readback is a narrower control.
pending_native_and_closure_gates.issue_84: Thousands of instrumented share/cancel cycles, stable Instruments/leaks allocations and ASan/concurrent native stress are still required; finite/source/compile evidence does not replace them.

scope.comparison: reviewed commit versus its immediate parent only

source_findings: Cargo adds a default-disabled appkit-lifecycle-tests feature and exactly one explicit harness=false, feature-required test target; original package, dependencies, JNI identity and release profiles remain unchanged.
The executable includes actual ../src/lib.rs and runs AppKit on the actual process Main thread, not Cargo test workers.
Removing the six-line test/feature inclusion from production macos.rs reproduces its parent bytes exactly.
AppKit owners remain on Main. Cross-thread exchanges contain owned Rust values, IDs and atomic counts.

Presented native cases capture Objective-C Weak<AnyObject> and Rust Weak<Completion> witnesses and assert release after queued cleanup. Pre-presentation cases use counts/admission evidence and have an empty weak-witness collection; they do not establish equivalent weak-owner proof.
CONTROL_FAILED independently records dispatched assertion panics, preventing the production panic catcher from manufacturing a passing control result.
Fresh exclusive per-process XML records only reached cases; a first failed ownership state prevents subsequent cases from running.
The finite batch selects eight cases. Separate stress_2048 remains outside the finite batch and has not executed.
Controlled actual native messages and Mail-service subject readback do not establish recipient or service-delivery acceptance.

The three Kotlin methods use default DesktopShareOwner through actual JNI/AppKit, an owned JFrame and a single-thread coroutine executor; no native-operation injection or virtual scheduler is used. Counts establish retained operations, not visible picker presentation.
Native outcome policy requires the exact three Kotlin methods/class once; only exact opposite-host skips are N/A. MacOS failure, headless/opt-out, missing, duplicate and unknown outcomes stay red.

Finite selectors must directly call macos_lifecycle_cases. The four-case existing registry and all original policy function semantics remain unchanged after removal of appended new-class handling, verified by AST comparison.
